It all began with the start of secondary school.
Et de la grande question du premier smar: And the big question of the first smartphone.
Tout a commencé lorsque mon fils de 11 a: It all started when my 11-year-old son began secondary school.
Comme beaucoup de ses camarades, il voul: Like many of his classmates, he wanted his first smartphone. But after talking it over with him, I realised it was mostly to play games on the bus.
Passionné d'électronique, je lui ai alor: Being an electronics enthusiast, I set him a challenge: {1}“What if we built our own games console?”
Avec l'aide de l'intelligence artificiel: With the help of artificial intelligence, we could even imagine and create our own games. That is how Brique was born.
Très vite, son petit frère de 7 ans a vo: Very soon his 7-year-old little brother wanted one too. My two boys became my first testers. Every morning we developed the games further, following their ideas and wishes.
Puis j'ai tenté une petite expérience :: Then I tried a little experiment: putting general-knowledge questions and school lessons right into the games. To reach the next level you had to answer correctly. Otherwise, you started again!
{1}Et à ma grande surprise, ils ont ador: {1}And to my great surprise, they loved it!
Ils se lançaient des défis, comparaient: They challenged each other, compared answers and learned without even noticing. The younger one kept trying to keep up with his big brother.
C'est là que j'ai compris que Brique pou: That is when I understood Brique could become much more than just a console.
Aujourd'hui, Brique grandit avec cette i: Today Brique is growing around that idea: giving children the fun of playing while sparking their curiosity and their desire to learn.
Une aventure née en famille, avec l'envi: An adventure born in a family, out of a wish to offer a different way to play.

It’s no match for a Switch, or even your sister’s calculator.
But can you explore its limits all the same?
Gauche, action, droite. Nous avons class: Left, action, right. We sorted 30 game genres by the controls they need: with 3 buttons almost everything stays playable; sometimes you just have to invent the way to play.
<b>Tels quels</b> : plateforme, course,: As is: platformer, racing, runner, bird between pipes, brick breaker, Pong, shooter, rhythm, Simon, stacker, quiz, choose-your-story, golf, fishing.
<b>En adaptant</b> : Snake et labyrinthe: With adaptation: Snake and maze (you turn left or right), Pac-Man, Tetris (the piece falls on its own), Sokoban, 2048, noughts and crosses (a cursor goes round the grid), RPG menus.
<b>Ce que 3 boutons font mieux</b> : le: What 3 buttons do better: two-player duels on a single console, one button each, and games you play without looking at your hands.
{1}La contrainte fait inventer.</b> « Co: {1}Constraints make you invent. “How do I make Pac-Man with 3 buttons?” is a real game-designer question: the child finds the answer, not the controller. A D-pad leads back to games that already exist; 3 buttons push towards games that don’t exist yet. It is also what makes the console recognisable: the 3-button console.
Classement fait par nos soins sur 30 gen: Ranking done by us across 30 common genres: a game-design estimate, not a study.

Français, maths, anglais, histoire, scie: French, maths, English, history, science… The lesson becomes the key to the game, revised with every play, including when playing a classmate’s game. You track the rate of correct answers per question.
